root_cause.text: Missing buffer head release (brelse) in error paths of ext4_fc_replay_inode() after a successful ext4_get_fc_inode_loc() call, because several failure branches jump directly to the 'out' label which only calls iput() but not brelse(), causing a buffer head reference leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "ext4_fc_replay_inode() calls ext4_get_fc_inode_loc() to get the inode location, which holds a reference to iloc.bh that must be released via brelse(). However, several error paths jump to the 'out' label without releasing iloc.bh: ext4_handle_dirty_metadata() failure, sync_dirty_buffer() failure, ext4_mark_inode_used() failure, ext4_iget() failure." The patch adds an 'out_brelse' label with brelse(iloc.bh) and redirects those error paths to it.

vuln_statements.explanation: This goto after ext4_handle_dirty_metadata failure jumps to 'out' instead of 'out_brelse', skipping the buffer head release.
This goto after sync_dirty_buffer failure jumps to 'out', omitting brelse and causing a buffer head leak.
This goto after ext4_mark_inode_used failure jumps to 'out' without brelse, leaking the buffer head.
This error path after ext4_iget failure jumps to 'out', bypassing the necessary brelse call.
